description: Metadata for curated and algorithm-generated district plans. Each entry includes metric scores for gallery display and comparison.

baseline.title: Current Enacted Map (2022)
baseline.note: Baseline for comparison. Metrics to be computed after data pipeline is complete.

plans.title: Straight-Line Split
plans.note: Each cut is the shortest straight line that divides the population in the right proportion, repeated until there are eight districts. It ignores counties and communities. Result: largest district is 0.43% from ideal, 49 county splits. For reference only, the 2020 presidential vote would have produced 5R-3D; partisan data was not used to draw the plan.

plans.title: Most Compact
plans.note: Starts from population-balanced round clusters, then minimizes total district boundary length while keeping every district within 1% of ideal population. Result: largest district is 0.51% from ideal, 20 county splits. For reference only, the 2020 presidential vote would have produced 6R-2D; partisan data was not used to draw the plan.

plans.title: Equal Population
plans.note: Starts from the Most Compact plan, then moves tracts to bring district populations as close to equal as possible, keeping shapes tidy. Result: largest district is 0.14% from ideal, 22 county splits. For reference only, the 2020 presidential vote would have produced 6R-2D; partisan data was not used to draw the plan.

plans.title: Keep Counties Whole
plans.note: Minimizes the number of split counties (and then boundary length) while keeping every district within 1% of ideal population. Result: largest district is 0.38% from ideal, 14 county splits. For reference only, the 2020 presidential vote would have produced 6R-2D; partisan data was not used to draw the plan.

note: Community-created plans will be added here as they are sourced from Dave's Redistricting App and other tools. Each plan will include a GeoJSON file path and pre-computed metric scores.
